zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions spatial relationships such as "directly left of", "directly right of", or "immediately left of", treat it as an adjacency constraint (difference of exactly one house) with the specified direction; do not allow larger gaps.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue describes a direct spatial relationship between two entities.
zebralogic.example: Treating "Carol is directly left of Arnold" as allowing any number of houses between them, which would place Carol far from Arnold.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating "N houses between X and Y" means there are exactly N houses separating X and Y, i.e., the absolute position difference is N+1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two entities.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "There is one house between the May birthday and the mother of Timothy" as adjacency (distance 1) instead of a distance of two houses.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say "X is somewhere left of Y" (or right of) impose only a strict ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or >) without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses the phrase "somewhere left of" or "somewhere right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "May birthday is somewhere to the left of January birthday" as requiring the two houses to be adjacent, which would incorrectly eliminate valid layouts.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "X is not in house 1"), remove that attribute from the candidate set for that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a negative statement about a location or attribute.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring a clue that says "The Yellow Monster smoker is not in house 1", leading to an illegal placement.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category (e.g., each name, each child, each birthday, each cigar) must appear exactly once across all houses; duplicates violate the puzzle constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously during solving, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the child name "Meredith" to two different houses, causing a conflict.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving capitalization and spelling; any alteration leads to a mismatch.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the final output stage, before submitting the answer.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "alice" instead of "Alice" for a child name, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately; this often triggers further deductions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After each round of constraint propagation, before moving on to speculative reasoning.
zebralogic.example: Failing to place the only possible house for the "Yellow Monster" smoker after other placements, leaving the puzzle under‑determined.

zebralogic.title: Interpret 'next to each other' as adjacency
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating that X and Y are "next to each other" means the two houses occupy consecutive positions (difference of 1), regardless of direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses the phrase "next to each other" or "are next to each other".
zebralogic.example: Treating the clue "The mother of Meredith and the Yellow Monster smoker are next to each other" as allowing any distance, which would place them far apart.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for name-attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly links a specific name to an attribute (e.g., "Eric is the Dunhill smoker"), enforce both directions: the named person must have that attribute, and that attribute must belong to that person.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a name together with another attribute.
zebralogic.example: Assigning Dunhill to a person other than Eric after a clue states "Eric is the Dunhill smoker", breaking the bidirectional link.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for attribute-attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly links two non‑name attributes (e.g., "The child named Meredith smokes Blends"), enforce both directions: the two attributes must belong to the same house, and each attribute's house must also have the other.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue equates two attributes without mentioning a name.
zebralogic.example: Treating "The child named Meredith smokes Blends" as only implying the Meredith child smokes Blends, but allowing the Blends smoker to have a different child.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Confusing the number of houses separating two entities with the absolute positional difference.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Add one to the given number when converting to a position difference; the distance between the houses is N+1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Overlooking that the two attributes must co‑occur in the same house, treating the clue as two separate constraints.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply both directions of the equivalence, ensuring the two attributes are assigned together.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: Forgetting to enforce that each value in a category appears exactly once across all houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After each assignment, check that the value has not already been used elsewhere in the same category.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Normalising text or overlooking case‑sensitivity requirements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Preserve the exact string as given in the problem when writing the final answer.
